claim: Experience cannot be transferred by recording one demonstration of a compound action. It transfers only when the demonstration is compiled into a NAMED PROCEDURE with a checked precondition and a read-back. Measured in this round, not asserted.
question_asked: 'Why can't we just give our model the most advanced coding actions and let him experience them once and then he will learn them?'

answer_no.one_sentence: Because in our own records a single episode contains ONE instance, and the thing that must generalise is the procedure. The episode is evidence; the procedure is the asset.

evidence.finding: r175: learn on episode 1, recall on episodes 2-5
evidence.why: memory is addressed by the sentence, and the sentence changes every episode

evidence.finding: r175: strip the operands, store one signature
evidence.why: what is left after the operands are removed is the procedure -- that is the unit that can transfer

evidence.finding: r180: five repairs as procedures (a loop, a whole-table pass, a timed sequence, a comparison, a question)
evidence.why: procedures are what moved the number; trajectories never did

evidence.finding: r179/r181: every regression this session came from a ROUTE, not from a missing action
evidence.result: drag-sort-numbers 1.00 -> 0.00; form-sequence 0/5 until the guard moved
evidence.why: the action was already known; the dispatch order was wrong. One demonstration would have shown the action, not the route.

external.single_demonstration: GEN-1.5 (Aug 2026) reports 59% on ten new tasks from one demonstration, but 83% after ten training steps -- the demonstration changes the weights, it does not act at inference. On an independent testbed (VLA-Arena, ICML 2026) six state-of-the-art models dropped to 0.00-0.01 when asked to chain two skills each had already mastered.
external.evaluation_noise: Bjarnason et al. 2026: ten identical full-benchmark replicates of the same system spanned 2.2-6.0 pp; two identical systems differ by three points about one time in six. Our own 650-trial SE is 1.90 pp and one repair is worth 0.77 pp.

what_a_one_shot_CAN_buy.how: write the PROCEDURE down as text a future run can read, with the precondition that selects it and the read-back that confirms it

arithmetic: At 650 trials one demonstration-recording repair is +0.77 pp and the noise band is 2.7 pp. A procedure that fixes a FAMILY (5 tasks) is +3.85 pp, which is just outside the band. That is why the batch rule exists and why 'once' has to mean 'once per shape', not 'once per task'.
structural_finding: VERB_PATTERNS is first-match-wins with ~24 entries and 21 goals match more than one pattern. r181 produced two more route defects of exactly that kind: SELECT above FORM_SEQUENCE swallowed 'Choose ... from the dropdown', and a page-shape guard in dispatch() ran before the verb table. Adding a capability does not add it -- it re-routes everything below it.
